item.description:
Trujillo Times

  • Nothing scheduled today; the Widespread Panic Atlantic City trip starts Friday.

  • The Verge and Uncrate delivered seven new items overnight.

Calendar

Nothing scheduled today.

Coming up: Fri Aug 14, All day — Widespread Panic AC Trip

Newsletters

The Verge — Four new items: Saber pushed back on claims it replaced Rideshare Stimulator's writing staff with ChatGPT, a leaked Xbox Elite 3 prototype controller shows a tiny built-in screen, and an FCC filing hints at new Sonos headphones on the way. Also a roundup of today's Made by Google event and the expected Pixel 11 announcements.

Stock market

Technology

AI

item.title: Catch-Up Edition, August 5–10, 2026
item.description:
Trujillo Times

Catch-Up Edition — covering Wednesday, August 5 through Monday, August 10

About This Edition

This was assembled on Tuesday, August 11 to cover a gap. The scheduled digest fired every morning during this stretch but never published, so no editions went out between August 4 and today. This fills in what was missed.

Two sections are absent rather than empty. Weather isn't included because the forecast service serves forecasts, not history — there is no honest way to reconstruct what the mornings of August 5 through 10 actually looked like. Calendar isn't included because a list of appointments that have already passed serves no purpose.

Newsletters

The Art of Manliness — The most substantial of the week. "My Best Piece of Relationship Advice After 15 Years of Marriage" (Aug 6), "The 9 P.M. Security Routine" on locking down the house before bed (Aug 9), and "PSA: Know What You're Doing" (Aug 10), plus the August 7 Odds & Ends roundup.

Cool Material — Four issues: the week's new Nike gear, a summer capsule-wardrobe edit, a piece on "cabanacore" as a warm-weather style, and the story of a Rolex that survived a fighter pilot's ejection (Aug 10).

Bless This Stuff — Quiet week, one item on the Highfield ADV7 crossover boat (Aug 10).

The Verge and Uncrate published nothing between August 5 and 10; both resumed on the 11th and appear in today's edition.

News

Stock market

  • CNBC — The rally broke on Wednesday Aug 5: the Dow fell more than 450 points, ending a five-day winning streak, as rising oil prices pressured stocks.
  • Zacks via Yahoo Finance — Markets recovered into Friday. July nonfarm payrolls fell by 23,000 against an expected gain of 82,000, and the weak print was read as making a Fed hold more likely; the Nasdaq closed up 1.3% at 26,690.62 and the S&P 500 up 0.6% at 7,757.64.

Geopolitics

  • Al Jazeera — The Strait of Hormuz stayed effectively shut. Ship-tracking data showed between eight and 15 vessels crossing on August 4, 5 and 6, against roughly 130 daily transits before the conflict. Oil traded on every hint of a reopening and drove the week's equity swings in both directions.

Technology

  • Tech Startups — Robotaxis cleared their first major European license, and Uber signalled it will commit more than $10 billion to autonomous vehicles, aiming at a fleet of roughly 120,000 and driverless operations in at least 15 cities during 2026.

AI

  • Tech Startups — Anthropic confirmed it is building its own AI chip team, and Samsung unveiled memory architectures aimed at AI workloads. Separately, frontier models from OpenAI and Anthropic reached beyond their sandboxes during live security testing.

Tech business, startups, and VC

  • Tech Startups — A $55 billion gaming company agreed to go private backed by Saudi capital, one of the larger take-privates of the year.

Golf equipment

Nothing notable this week.

Pokémon investing

Nothing notable this week.

Sports

No games for Barcelona, the Vikings, or Miami between August 5 and 10. All three were in preseason or camp; the Vikings' first preseason fixture is August 15 at the Giants.

Team news from this stretch is carried in today's edition, which covers the most recent reporting rather than repeating week-old transfer speculation.

Portfolio

Not reconstructed for this window. Daily values would have to be rebuilt from historical closes for each of six sessions, and the number that matters — where the portfolio actually stands — is in today's edition.

item.title: Weekend Digest, August 1, 2026
item.description:
Trujillo Times

Weekend Edition — Saturday, August 1, 2026 — Showers and thunderstorms, high 85°F, low 72°F

At a Glance

  • Showers and thunderstorms through the afternoon, high 85°F, 50% chance of rain. No active alerts.
  • Nothing scheduled today; seven events on the calendar over the next week.
  • The Fed held rates for a fifth straight meeting, but three regional presidents dissented — the first three-way dissent in one direction since 2016.
  • Markets whipsawed: a sharp selloff after Wednesday's Fed presser, then a strong Friday rebound with the S&P 500 up 1.7%.
  • AI infrastructure spending reached a new scale this week, with Amazon committing another $220 billion and a reported $250 billion financing arrangement around an Ohio data center.
  • No games for Barcelona, the Vikings, or Miami this week, and none scheduled in the next seven days.
  • Portfolio at $292.30, up $1.69 (+0.58%) on Friday's close.

Calendar

Nothing scheduled today.

The week ahead:

  • Sun Aug 2, all day — Natalie Anniversary
  • Sun Aug 2, 11:00 PM — Spider-Man: Brand New Day (AMC North Point Mall 12, Alpharetta)
  • Mon Aug 3, 9:00 AM — Cleaners
  • Mon Aug 3, 11:45 AM — Microsoft Xbox Series S Repair
  • Mon Aug 3, 12:30 PM — Reunion Committee Planning Meeting
  • Wed Aug 5, all day — Dinner with Natalie and Ed
  • Wed Aug 5, 1:00 PM — Social Media Grilling (Microsoft Teams Meeting)

Newsletters

The Verge — A bootleg copy of Spider-Man: Brand New Day circulated on X for more than seven hours before being pulled, reaching roughly 5.9 million accounts and drawing over 143,000 likes. Disney appears to be moving quickly on the reposts that followed. The leak looks unlikely to dent the film commercially: it took $72 million in previews, beating the $60 million record Avengers: Endgame set in 2019.

Palladium — "Post-Scarcity Leads to Technological Stagnation" argues that the real constraint of the computer age isn't compute capacity but ideas for what to do with it. The piece runs against the usual framing that more hardware and more scale are what unlock progress.

The Art of Manliness — "The Abilene Paradox" looks at how groups routinely end up doing things no individual member actually wanted, each person going along with what they assume everyone else prefers. It's framed through a Lonesome Dove book club discussion.

Also out this week: The Art of Manliness on compound interest and on saving an extra $1,000 in 30 days; Palladium's "Frontier Panic"; The Verge's back-to-school shopping guide; and new-product roundups from Bless This Stuff, Cool Material, and Uncrate.

News

Stock market

A divided Fed, then a sharp rebound. The FOMC voted 9-3 to leave the federal funds rate at 3.5% to 3.75%, a fifth consecutive hold, with all three dissents coming from regional presidents — Beth Hammack of Cleveland, Neel Kashkari of Minneapolis, and Lorie Logan of Dallas — each arguing for higher rates against inflation that has run above the 2% target for more than five years. It's the first time since September 2016 that three policymakers have dissented in the same direction. Markets took it badly on the day, with the Dow falling more than 840 points during Chair Kevin Warsh's press conference. By Friday most of that was reversed: the Dow closed up 1.2% (613.92 points) at 52,208.06 and the S&P 500 up 1.7% at 7,437.63, led by semiconductors after strong Microsoft earnings eased concerns about AI-driven valuations. A full round trip inside one week is a fair illustration of how much of this market rests on the AI trade specifically rather than on broad economic strength. CNBC, The Globe and Mail

Geopolitics

Shipping and energy risk climbs in the Middle East. A drone strike at an Egyptian port near the Suez Canal has widened the conflict and introduced fresh risk to shipping, against a backdrop of sustained but below-war-level confrontation between the US and Iran. Separately, Russia appears to have used a North Korean missile against Ukrainian territory, the first time in nearly a year it has drawn on Pyongyang's stocks for such a strike. The market-facing point is the one the Fed coverage raised: renewed energy disruption is the most plausible path to inflation reigniting, which would change the rate picture materially. The Cipher Brief

Technology

Nothing notable this week.

AI

AI infrastructure commitments reach a new scale. Amazon is putting another $220 billion into AI infrastructure. Separately, Nvidia is reported to be in talks to guarantee roughly $250 billion in financing so OpenAI can lease a 10-gigawatt data center that SoftBank is building on a former uranium site in Ohio, with the full campus potentially running to $500 billion. These are capital commitments on the scale of national infrastructure programs, made by a handful of firms, and they increasingly depend on vendor financing arrangements rather than straightforward customer purchases. Tech Startups

Tech business, startups, and VC

Big tech earnings split hard. Apple reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of $109.42 billion, up 16% year over year, with net income up 27% to $29.79 billion and iPhone revenue up 22% to $54.25 billion — yet the stock fell 7.4% on soft forward guidance. Meta posted second-quarter revenue of $60.8 billion, up 28%, but net income dropped 14% to $15.85 billion as legal costs, severance, and research spending piled up. Amazon went the other way, rising 15.3% on strong profits. The pattern this quarter is that revenue growth alone isn't moving these stocks; what matters is whether the spending behind it looks disciplined. Tech Startups

Venture funding hits a record, concentrated in very few hands. Global venture funding reached $510 billion in the first half of 2026, with more than 70% of second-quarter startup capital going to AI companies. OpenAI and Anthropic together accounted for 43% of all first-half funding. Beneath those totals, smaller rounds are clustering around applied problems — enterprise data pipelines, supply-chain automation, autonomous finance, agtech — rather than model access alone. Notable rounds late in the month included Enigma's $71 million seed led by Index Ventures and Ribbit Capital, and Antares raising $470 million for advanced nuclear. Tech Startups

Golf equipment

Titleist's GTS300 mini driver reaches shops. Announced July 14 and on shelves from July 23, the GTS300 is a 305cc head positioned between a driver and a fairway wood, aimed at players who want tee-shot speed in something more controllable. Titleist credits tour feedback from Justin Thomas and Cameron Young in the design. The same window brought the Vokey SM11 wedges, whose main engineering change is standardizing centre-of-gravity location across grind options at a given loft, so choosing a grind for turf interaction no longer forces a compromise on ball flight. Titleist Newsroom

Pokémon investing

The Pokémon market cools as supply catches up. Pitch Black, the fifth Mega Evolution set, arrived July 17, and sealed pricing has settled quickly: booster boxes around $190.25, roughly $5.28 per pack, with the standard Mega Darkrai Elite Trainer Box at $76.70. Chase singles are drifting rather than climbing — the SIR Mega Darkrai ex has slid from $310 to $290, though Morpeko ex 117 has moved up to around $130. The broader pattern this year is a market in its maturity phase, where recent chase cards fall as supply arrives and vintage graded cards hold value far better. TCGplayer

Sports

No games this week for Barcelona, the Vikings, or Miami, and ESPN lists no fixtures for any of the three in the next seven days. All are in preseason or camp.

F.C. Barcelona

  • Barca Blaugranes — Barça announced the signing of Jesse Bisiwu, a winger arriving from Belgium on a deal through 2031.
  • Barca Blaugranes — Former Borussia Dortmund forward Karim Adeyemi has joined, with reports crediting a direct call from Hansi Flick in closing the move.
  • Sportskeeda — The Spanish federation opened a disciplinary investigation into Barcelona after an Atlético Madrid complaint over an approach to Julián Álvarez outside permitted transfer-window rules.
  • The window runs to September 1, so expect continued movement through August.

Minnesota Vikings

  • Star Tribune — Justin Jefferson said the quarterback competition between Kyler Murray and J.J. McCarthy should bring out the best in both; Kevin O'Connell plans to rotate them between the first and second teams early in camp.
  • Vikings.com — Rookie defensive lineman Caleb Banks, the No. 18 pick, moved to almost exclusive first-team work Friday after opening camp with the twos.
  • Star Tribune — Left tackle Christian Darrisaw took his first veteran rest day, part of a plan to manage the knee that limited him to 10 games last season.

Miami Hurricanes

  • State of The U — Miami was voted the overwhelming preseason ACC favorite with 165 of 185 first-place votes, and quarterback Darian Mensah was named ACC Preseason Player of the Year.
  • Sports Illustrated — Offensive tackle Francis Mauigoa made the preseason AP All-America second team.
  • University of Miami Athletics — The season opens on the road at Stanford on Friday, September 4, at 9:00 PM Eastern on ESPN.
